The Dreamer’s sweep

live contracts checked 2026-08-20

Dreamer is a seeded teammate with an enabled every 1d loop. Each sweep marks suspect memories from pinned evidence, then consolidates the working set without erasing its history.

Run the sweep

You drive one truthful replay. Watch the active set shrink from three memories to two while every predecessor and every challenge stays legible in the graph.

1 / 6
  1. Before the sweep, Juniper remembers three memories.
  2. The enabled Dreamer loop begins its MARK phase.
  3. An evidence-bearing message is pinned at version 4.
  4. The message creates disputes edges to two suspect memory predecessors; neither memory is edited or deleted.
  5. CONSOLIDATE creates one successor memory with supersedes edges to both predecessors.
  6. Juniper’s remembers edges move from the two predecessors to the successor. The active set shrinks from three memories to two, while the predecessors, disputes, and supersedes relations remain in the ledger.

This is a seeded lifecycle loop, not human gardening. You are replaying what Dreamer does. The active set is mutable; the historical record is not a wastebasket.

01Two phases, two kinds of truth

MARK makes doubt explicit and cheap. CONSOLIDATE pays for a clearer memory only after evidence exists.

MARKdoes not rewrite

Evidence disputes a claim

A message or memory may source disputes. The target may be any entity, but the edge cannot exist without evidence-shaped properties.

quote
The exact evidence excerpt.
expected / observed
The contradiction, stated in both directions.
pinnedVersion
The target version the evidence evaluated.
CONSOLIDATEwrites a successor

A new memory becomes the head

A memory may supersedes another memory. The required reason explains the replacement; reads resolve to the chain head.

supersedes
Successor → predecessor; acyclic and retained.
reason
Required on every successor edge.
remembers
Holder → memory; mutable so the active set can be corrected.

02What the sweep keeps

The distinction is structural: working-set edges can move, while the memory record and its evidence trail remain.

The memories

Both predecessors remain as memory entities after their successor becomes current.

The reasons

disputes and supersedes preserve why the working set changed.

The database rule

Memory deletion is refused. Consolidation creates lineage; it never turns history into absence.

tm8 Help · Foundation · v2

Design foundation

The shared design layer every tm8 Help artifact is built on. This page is the spec and the living demo at once: every token, component, convention and motion rule below is rendered by the same foundation block you will copy into your artifact. Read it once; a fresh session with no other context should produce work indistinguishable in style from the rest of the fleet.

Solid ink — shipped, true of tm8 today Ghost ink — designed, not built (dashed, faded) verified against contract doc 01a0155c… on 2026-08-20

The grammar, playing

One replay, twice. Both panels step through the same five frames — a space, a task, a session, a doc, a message — using the graph-node language, the edge lines, and the standard control cluster every Help artifact reuses. The left panel moves; the right panel is the prefers-reduced-motion variant: same knowledge, no animation. Motion starts, teaches, settles — play runs once to the end and stops.

Full motion — nodes arrive, edges draw

This node style — icon, title, small-caps kind, hairline stroke on a shallow-radius surface — is the graph-node language of the whole fleet, matching Section 0's replay. A live session carries a green dot; it pulses only while motion is allowed.

01The token sheet, live

The v2 sheet, rendered by this page right now. Warm paper, warm near-black ink, one bronze accent — the same family as the product’s own brass, so replicas and Help pages finally read as one thing. The page follows your OS theme via prefers-color-scheme; each tile names both values. Every color on every Help artifact comes from this sheet — per-artifact content colors are derived from --accent, --accent-2 and the state colors, never invented hexes.

Foundation constants (motion + ghost ink)

Kept from v1, deliberately — they were right. Micro feedback --dur-fast: 120ms, state changes --dur-base: 180ms, scene changes --dur-slow: 280ms; default easing --ease-out: cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1). Ghost ink is --ghost-opacity: 0.62 with dash pattern 5 4.

Type, spacing, radius

h1 · 42 / regular

h2 · 28 / medium

h3 · 19.5 / semibold

body · 16.5 / 1.62 · Charter → Iowan Old Style → Georgia. System serifs only — no webfonts. The bigger the text, the lighter it sets.

code · 13.5 · ui-monospace stack

labels · 10–11 mono · uppercase · letterspaced

caption · italic 13.5 muted — captions state the point

Spacing — 4px grid: 4 / 8 / 12 / 16 / 24 / 32 / 48 / 64. Section gaps 48–64px, card padding 18–22px, prose ≤ 68ch, content column 1040px.

Radius — 4px cards, panels and plates, 3px buttons and inputs, 999px pills and chips. Borders — 1px var(--line) hairlines; var(--line-strong) where an edge must hold (graph nodes, the masthead rule, control bars).

Elevation — none. No card shadows; hairlines and the mat carry depth. The only solid dark field on a page is the terminal canvas.

02The shared component vocabulary

Each component below is live — inspect it, tab to it, hover it. Class names are stable; reuse them as-is.

Terminal block .term

The signature component. Always dark in both themes, matted in a paper frame like a book plate. The bar names the real context (workspace — session) with a PTY tag — no traffic-light dots; this is a stream, not a mac window. Prompts are prefixed $ by CSS (.p) in bronze; output is plain (.out). Every command shown must be real syntax; every output shaped like what the CLI actually prints.

Cards, panels, pills, buttons

Card .card — surface, hairline, 4px radius, no shadow. Panel .panel is the same at 22px padding for interactive widgets. Plate .plate mats a replica or figure with an italic caption.

neutral working blocked? cancelled live

Pills are stroked, never filled. State is never color-only: color pairs with text; dots add shape (solid = running, hollow = declared, pulsing = live).

Buttons and links — real <button> and <a> only, and always outlined, never filled: the primary wears the bronze stroke. Hover tints and strengthens the stroke, never color alone; focus is a visible 2px bronze outline.

A link

Anything clickable looks clickable: a bronze stroke or underline, pointer cursor, hover state, visible focus.

Identity chips .who — member vs teammate

The fleet-wide identity device, matching the product: a member (human) wears a circular avatar; a teammate (agent) wears a 5px rounded-square avatar. Shape carries the distinction, color supports it — never color alone. Members tint slate, teammates tint bronze.

MVMara Voss member JUJuniper teammate DIDispatcher teammate

Entity-kind icons

The real icon set from the product UI: 16×16, stroke-only currentColor at 1.4px, round caps. All 21 registered kinds, plus the diamond fallback for custom c: kinds. Use them wherever an entity appears — lists, nodes, chips.

Edge lines

Edges are 1.2px lines in --muted, labeled in 9.5px mono with the real edge type name. Bronze marks the edge currently being taught. Ghost dashes mark designed-not-built relations.

03Two inks: the honesty devices

Truth is the floor. Three devices keep every artifact honest, and each has one job:

  • The two-inks legend .ink-legend — place it once, near the top, on ANY page that shows anything unbuilt. Solid ink = shipped and true today. Ghost ink (dashed border or dashed stroke at --ghost-opacity) = designed, not built. The same pair renders Craft's node grammar in Section 7: ref nodes solid (they point at entities that exist), spec nodes ghost (they sketch entities to be born).
  • The honest-gap card .gap-card — for a real limitation of shipped tm8, stated in the product's own words. Not for roadmap; that is ghost ink's job.
  • The verified stamp .stamp — on claims harvested from a live node or the CLI catalog, with the date. The footer of every artifact carries one.

Solid vs ghost, on nodes (Craft ref/spec grammar)

Honest gap. Full-text search is reserved and honestly unavailable — the CLI says so itself. Use entity query and graph query instead.

verified on 2026-08-20 against tm8 help + live node

The gap card and stamp above are the components themselves, not pictures of them.

04The animation grammar

Motion explains; it never merely decorates. The operational rules, fleet-wide:

  • Starts, teaches, settles. Every animation runs once toward a resting state that still carries the lesson. Nothing loops forever demanding attention. The only sanctioned repeat is the 1.6s liveness pulse on a live session dot — and it stops under reduced motion.
  • Quick and eased. Use the named durations: --dur-fast 120ms (hover, press), --dur-base 180ms (reveal, toggle), --dur-slow 280ms (a node arriving, an edge drawing). Default easing --ease-out; use --ease-standard for symmetric moves. Longer sequences are built from steps of these, driven by the stepper.
  • Banned: bouncing, confetti, parallax, autoplaying infinite loops, motion that exists only to impress. If it does not teach, cut it.
  • Reduced motion is a variant, not a fallback. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce the foundation kills every animation and transition globally; your widget must still work as a stepper of still frames (the centrepiece above shows both side by side). Never autoplay when reduced motion is on — the foundation script refuses for you.
  • The control cluster is standard. Play / Step / scrub-range / frame counter, in that order, wired by TM8.stepper(). One way to drive every sequence in the fleet, so a reader who learns it once can drive everything.

Starts–teaches–settles, in one gesture: press the button; the edge draws once at --dur-slow, the caption lands, and the scene rests.

05Interaction grammar: one way each

Builders invent these divergently unless they are named. There is exactly ONE way to do each of the following, demoed live:

Hover-reveal .reveal

An inline term carrying a quiet definition. Dashed accent underline, help cursor, tooltip on hover AND on keyboard focus (tabindex="0"). Try it: a teammateAn agent persona — durable, does not run. “A teammate is who, a session is now.” is not a sessionOne running instance of a teammate — a real process in a real terminal.. Use it for vocabulary, never for essential content.

The “what you type / what comes back” toggle .toggle2

Two real buttons with aria-pressed, swapping two panes. The pressed button doubles its bronze stroke and tints — never a fill. One toggle per exchange; never tabs for this.

tm8 entity context 01a09f21-4c00-7a11-8b2e-0d3f5a7c9e11 --format json

  "schemaVersion": "tm8.entity-context.v1",

            "title": "Fix login redirect loop", "version": 4, … },
  "content": { "excerpt": "…", "truncated": false },

The control cluster .tmc + TM8.stepper()

Already driving the centrepiece above. Markup: .tmc-play, .tmc-step, an input[type=range].tmc-scrub, and .tmc-count. Wire it with TM8.stepper(root, { frames, render, intervalMs }); the script handles play-to-end-and-stop, keyboard scrubbing, and the reduced-motion refusal to autoplay. Do not build your own player.

06Looking like the product: the replica kit

When an artifact depicts the tm8 UI — a board, a thread, a terminal — it uses these replicas, distilled from the real components in packages/tm8-ui/src. They live inside a .pn frame that carries the product's own token palette (warm paper, brass brand), so demos read as the real product while the page around them stays on the contract sheet. Add .pn--dark for the product's dark theme. Everything inside the frames below is populated from the shared mock workspace (§7).

Task board — columns, cards, status pills

Column: card surface, hairline, 8px radius, uppercase mono header. Card: 7px radius, 12.5px/550 title, mono acceptance count. Status pills are 9.5px mono on soft tints; categories are law (to_do | in_progress | done | cancelled), statuses are words.

Panel tabs · entity chips · liveness

Task discussion — message bubbles with structural identity

Human turns are bordered bubbles on the card surface; your own turns align right; agent turns render as an open reading column. The byline carries the avatar — circle for members, 5px square for teammates — so authorship is visible at a glance and in the markup.

Terminal strip — a session's chrome

The strip is product surface (34px, avatar square, name, provider in mono); the canvas below is always near-black in both themes, because the terminal is a real PTY.

Fonts: the product ships Newsreader / Hanken Grotesk / JetBrains Mono; artifacts are webfont-free by contract, so replicas render on the system stacks — closest honest rendering, noted here once.

07The mock workspace: Northlake

Every Help artifact depicts the SAME fictional workspace, so the fleet reads as one product in one team. It ships as TM8_MOCK inside the foundation script — the board and thread above are rendered from it. Do not invent your own cast; extend Northlake if a section needs more.

The rules of the mock

  • Ids are v7-shaped and start 01a0… — real-shaped, never real.
  • Field shapes mirror the live DTOs (tm8 entity context --format json is the reference): tasks carry state.status/priority/assignees/assignments/acceptance/completionGate, entities carry version and counters with humanMessages/agentMessages distinct.
  • Statuses use the contract spellings: open | pulled | working | in_review | blocked | cancelled | done.
  • Teammate model strings are NOT invented — mock teammates carry only their provider (claude-code / codex); harvest exact model ids from the live catalog if a section needs them.

08Page anatomy: the fill-in template

Every Help artifact has exactly this shape (contract §4). The reader reaches the centrepiece within one screen; everything after it is quiet and supports it.

index.html — skeleton
<a class="skip" href="#main">Skip to content</a>      <!-- first element in body -->
<header class="site">
  <span class="brand">tm8 Help</span>
  <span class="crumb">/ ‹Artifact title›</span>
  <span class="hub-note">Part of <strong>tm8 Help</strong> — open the hub
    from your tm8 artifacts list</span>          <!-- words, NEVER a hyperlink -->
</header>
<main id="main">
  <h1>‹Artifact title›</h1>                      <!-- the only h1 -->
  <p class="lede">‹One or two sentences: what this teaches, who it is for.›</p>
  <!-- ink legend here IF anything unbuilt appears below -->
  <section> ‹THE centrepiece — one strong idea, controls wired by TM8.stepper› </section>
  <section> ‹quiet supporting sections: prose ≤70ch, inline demos, gap cards› </section>
</main>
<footer class="site">Last updated ‹date› · ‹Artifact name› · tm8 Help v1 ·
  ‹verified stamp›</footer>

No cross-artifact hyperlinks, ever — preview URLs expire. Name siblings by title only, marked data-help-role="sibling". Self-contained single file: all CSS and JS inline, no CDNs, no fonts, no fetch.

09Voice

  • Second person, present tense, short and concrete. Verbs first: “You spawn a session; the task is its first instruction.”
  • Captions state the point, not the picture: write “no copies — it's a graph”, not “diagram showing three collections”.
  • No marketing language. Banned words: powerful, seamless, simply, magic. No exclamation marks.
  • Command names, flags, ids, statuses in <code>. American spelling, consistently.
  • Every sentence answers something a real user asks; if it doesn't, cut it.

10The builder checklist

Run these ten checks before calling any Help artifact done. They are the contract's five gates plus foundation conformance.

  1. ONE interactive centrepiece the reader drives, reached within one screen.
  2. The page teaches through motion, state or manipulation — not a documentation wall.
  3. Every claim is true of tm8 today; every command is real syntax; every output is real-shaped. Unbuilt things wear ghost ink with the legend present.
  4. The foundation block is verbatim: the v2 token sheet first, no invented hexes, no webfonts, no frameworks, single self-contained file.
  5. Product depictions use the .pn replica kit and the Northlake mock workspace — same cast, same ids, DTO-true shapes.
  6. Motion follows the grammar: named durations and easings, starts-teaches-settles, nothing loops forever, nothing banned.
  7. prefers-reduced-motion yields a genuine still-frame variant; nothing autoplays under it.
  8. Everything mouse-drivable is keyboard-drivable; focus is visible everywhere; semantics are real (button, a, one h1, ordered headings).
  9. Contrast ≥ 4.5:1 text / 3:1 UI in both themes; no color-only state.
  10. Skeleton, voice and honesty devices match this page; footer carries the date stamp; no cross-artifact links. Would you show it as an example of good work?

11The copy-paste foundation block

One button, three parts, lifted verbatim from this very page: the foundation <style> (tokens + every component above), the #tm8-icons SVG defs (all 21 kinds), and the foundation <script> (reduced-motion helper, TM8.stepper, toggle wiring, TM8_MOCK). Paste them into your artifact's index.html and build on top — the copy is generated from the live blocks, so it can never drift from the spec.

12Builder notes (truth floor, applied)

  • Mock data is fine and expected. Northlake is fiction. What must be REAL is the shapes (DTO-true fields), the syntax (every command from tm8 help), and the behaviours depicted (things tm8 actually does). Fiction in the nouns, truth in the verbs.
  • Never let an animation smuggle in a nonexistent feature — if the sequence shows it happening, tm8 must do it, or it wears ghost ink.
  • Harvest at build time what this foundation cannot fix: real CLI output for your section's commands, exact model ids, edge legality from tm8 edge type list.
  • Where the contract is silent, this foundation has chosen (durations, ghost constants, identity shapes, the .pn replica layer); where the contract speaks, it wins.

What v2 changed, and why

  • An editorial voice on system stacks. Display and body set in the system serifs (Iowan Old Style / Palatino / Charter / Georgia) — the bigger the text, the lighter it sets. Labels, kinds and figures stay mono. No webfonts, as the contract demands.
  • Color re-grounded in the product. The Help accent is now bronze (#A97B2F), harmonizing with tm8-ui’s own brass (#B26A2B) and warm paper — replicas no longer clash with the pages that frame them. The second series moved teal → slate (#54708D) so gold stays the only warm accent.
  • Stroke, not fill. Buttons are outlined, pills are stroked, rules and underlines carry the accent. The only solid dark field on any page is the terminal canvas — which is the point.
  • Sharper edges. Radius 10px → 4px; card shadows removed. Hairlines carry depth.
  • The terminal re-cut. Matted plate frame, a named bar (workspace — session) with a PTY tag instead of traffic-light dots — instantly “tm8 Help”, not “a mac window”.
  • The control cluster machined into one instrument — a single bordered transport bar: play / step / scrub / tabular counter.
  • Kept from v1, deliberately: motion constants 120/180/280ms and easings, ghost ink 0.62 + 5 4 dash, identity shapes (circle = member, rounded square = teammate), the 21 harvested icons, the Northlake mock, the replica kit, and the self-generating copy block.
